title: The till
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Gully offers the shack's till. Wood refuses before Gully finishes the sentence. Gully finishes it anyway: 'for the copies, not for you.' Wood still refuses. The uncle says take it; Wood says no to the uncle too, which nobody does. The uncle nods.

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY with the cash drawer open, a hand in it. WOOD in the door, already shaking his head. BARNABY. The UNCLE.

image.prompt: a teenager with his hand in an open cash drawer in a bait shack while a young man in the doorway shakes his head, an old man watching, black and white, no words
an old weathered man on a crab pot, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Gully looking at Wood. Nobody says no to the uncle. The uncle looking at Wood too.

image.prompt: a teenager and an old man both looking at a young man in a doorway who has just refused, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle nodding once. The drawer closing. That's it. Wood's no held, and the uncle liked it. The strip would rather have the nod than the money and says so by drawing the nod big.
